Identify and list all current FDA-approv.title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapies to Treat Patients with Sickle Cell Disease
Identify and list all current FDA-approv.summary: The FDA has approved two milestone treatments, Casgevy and Lyfgenia, representing the first cell-based gene therapies for the treatment of sickle cell disease (SCD) in patients 12 years and older. Casgevy is the first FDA-approved therapy utilizing CRISPR/Cas9, a type of genome editing technology.
key_points: Casgevy is approved for the treatment of sickle cell disease in patients 12 years of age and older with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises.
Casgevy is the first FDA-approved therapy utilizing CRISPR/Cas9, a type of genome editing technology.
Patients' hematopoietic (blood) stem cells are modified by genome editing using CRISPR/Cas9 technology.
The modified blood stem cells are transplanted back into the patient where they engraft (attach and multiply) within the bone marrow and increase the production of fetal hemoglobin (HbF).

Identify and list all current FDA-approv.title: World's First CRISPR-Based Gene Therapy Approved by FDA
Identify and list all current FDA-approv.summary: The FDA has approved the first CRISPR-based gene therapy for sickle cell disease, which employs CRISPR gene editing to edit genes in patients' hematopoietic stem cells. The therapy, exa-cel, is developed by Vertex Pharmaceuticals and CRISPR Therapeutics.
key_points: The FDA has approved the first CRISPR-based gene therapy for sickle cell disease.
The therapy, exa-cel, employs CRISPR gene editing to edit genes in patients' hematopoietic stem cells.
Exa-cel is developed by Vertex Pharmaceuticals and CRISPR Therapeutics.
The therapy has been approved for the treatment of sickle cell disease in patients 12 years of age and older.

Identify and list all current FDA-approv.summary: The FDA has unveiled a new approval pathway for bespoke gene therapies, which will allow for the approval of custom CRISPR therapies. The pathway focuses on genome editing and RNA-based methods that target the underlying cause of a rare disease.
key_points: The FDA has unveiled a new approval pathway for bespoke gene therapies.
The pathway focuses on genome editing and RNA-based methods that target the underlying cause of a rare disease.
The pathway will allow for the approval of custom CRISPR therapies.
The FDA will continue to gather data post-market to ensure safety.

Analyze the technical differences and si.title: Comparison of CRISPR/Cas9 and Cas12a for gene editing in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
Analyze the technical differences and si.summary: This study compares the efficiency and precision of CRISPR-Cas9 and Cas12a systems in gene editing in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii. The results show that Cas9 targets more sites than Cas12a, but Cas12a shows higher precision in single-strand templated DNA repair and gene editing.
key_points: Cas9 targets 8-32 times more sites than Cas12a in promoter regions and coding sequences.
Cas12a shows higher precision in single-strand templated DNA repair and gene editing.
Cas9 and Cas12a RNPs with ssODN templates induce similar total editing levels.
Cas12a requires a T-rich PAM, while Cas9 recognizes a G-rich PAM.

Analyze the technical differences and si.title: Alt-R CRISPR-Cas9 vs Cas12a systems | IDT
Analyze the technical differences and si.summary: This article compares the Alt-R CRISPR-Cas9 and Cas12a systems, highlighting their differences in PAM recognition and guide RNA requirements. Cas12a requires a T-rich PAM and a one-part gRNA, while Cas9 recognizes a G-rich PAM and uses a two-part guide RNA.
key_points: Cas12a requires a T-rich PAM, while Cas9 recognizes a G-rich PAM.
Cas12a uses a one-part gRNA, while Cas9 uses a two-part guide RNA.
Cas12a is suitable for targeting AT-rich regions, while Cas9 is more efficient for targeting GC-rich regions.
Cas12a can recognize many TTTT PAM sites in addition to TTTV motifs.

Analyze the technical differences and si.title: Activities and specificities of CRISPR/Cas9 and Cas12a nucleases in plant genome editing
Analyze the technical differences and si.summary: This study compares the activities and specificities of CRISPR-Cas9 and Cas12a nucleases in plant genome editing. The results show that Cas12a has distinct features, including a T-rich PAM requirement and the ability to process multiple crRNAs from an array.
key_points: Cas12a requires a T-rich PAM, while Cas9 recognizes a G-rich PAM.
Cas12a can process multiple crRNAs from an array, simplifying multiplex gene editing.
Cas12a has a higher efficiency than Cas9 for targeting AT-rich regions.
Cas12a induces double-stranded breaks with a 4-5 bp overhang.

Analyze the technical differences and si.summary: This article compares the Cas9 and Cas12a systems, highlighting their differences in cutting mechanisms and multiplexing capabilities. Cas12a leaves staggered cuts with 5' overhangs, while Cas9 creates blunt double-stranded breaks.
key_points: Cas12a leaves staggered cuts with 5' overhangs, while Cas9 creates blunt double-stranded breaks.
Cas12a has a higher multiplexing capability than Cas9.
Cas12a is more precise and can guide more predictable repair processes.

Map the intellectual property landscape.title: CRISPR technology: Patent & License landscapes
Map the intellectual property landscape.summary: This report provides an overview of the CRISPR patent and license landscape, focusing on genetically modified plants. It highlights key points such as the number of patent families covering CRISPR-related technology, priority filings in China and the USA, and licensing agreements.
key_points: There are over 17,900 patent families covering CRISPR-related technology.
Over 14,900 have claims covering genome editing.
46% of CRISPR patents have priority filings in China, and nearly 40% have them in the USA.
Two groups, CVC and Broad, hold issued foundational CRISPR-Cas9 patents.
Broad's patent protection applies only to eukaryotes, is subject to multiple challenges, and has a reduced scope in Europe.

Map the intellectual property landscape.title: The emerging patent landscape of CRISPR–Cas gene editing
Map the intellectual property landscape.summary: This report provides an overview of the emerging patent landscape of CRISPR-Cas gene editing, highlighting key players and patent holders. It notes that commercial assignees have taken less ground in the early phases of the CRISPR-Cas patent landscape.
key_points: The top ten patent holders in the CRISPR-Cas patent landscape are MIT, Harvard College, the Broad Institute, and others.
MIT is on top, followed by Harvard College and the Broad Institute.
The list of the top ten patent holders is based on a search of key words CRISPR and Cas9 in the patent database from Thomson Innovation.
The number of total inventions represents separate patent families where each family represents one unique invention.

Map the intellectual property landscape.title: Why IP Strategy Matters in CRISPR-Based Therapies
Map the intellectual property landscape.summary: This article highlights the importance of IP strategy in CRISPR-based therapies, noting that foundational patents are primarily owned by institutions like the University of California, Berkeley and the Broad Institute.
key_points: Foundational patents are primarily owned by institutions like the University of California, Berkeley and the Broad Institute.
These institutions hold the rights to pivotal technologies like CRISPR-Cas9, shaping how licensing agreements are managed.
The dispute over which institute first discovered and developed technologies like CRISPR-Cas9 has prompted legal battles, influencing licensing terms globally.

Map the intellectual property landscape.title: [PDF] CRISPR Technology 2025: Patent & License landscape on Plants
Map the intellectual property landscape.summary: This report provides a comprehensive analysis of the patent and licensing landscape for CRISPR-based technologies applied to plants, with a particular focus on genome-edited crops and non-transgenic approaches.
key_points: The landscape is still developing, with room for further innovation.
Many patents cover both transgenic and non-transgenic approaches, and boundaries are not always clearly defined.
European applicants include KWS Saat and Tropic Biosciences, but remain few.
Most EP filings come from US-based actors (e.g. Corteva, Pairwise, Broad).

Map the intellectual property landscape.title: CRISPR and Gene Editing Patents: What Biotech Startups Must Know
Map the intellectual property landscape.summary: This article highlights the importance of understanding the CRISPR patent landscape for biotech startups, noting that securing patents is only one part of the equation.
key_points: Startups need to consider how they will navigate licensing and collaboration opportunities with existing patent holders.
Securing licenses to use core CRISPR technology, especially CRISPR-Cas9, can involve significant costs but also opens up opportunities for collaboration.

A well-executed patent landscape analysis provides a clear picture of the existing patents in the CRISPR domain, identifying areas where there may be freedom to operate and areas where potential conflicts could arise.

Map the intellectual property landscape.title: CRISPR-Cas: Navigating the Patent Landscape to Explore Boundless Applications
Map the intellectual property landscape.summary: This article highlights the complex and competitive patent landscape of CRISPR-Cas technology, noting that a high-profile litigation between two major groups is central to the contour of the patent landscape.
key_points: The University of California, Berkeley, the University of Vienna, and Dr. Emmanuelle Charpentier (collectively known as CVC) claim ownership of the fundamental inventions related to CRISPR-Cas9.
The Broad Institute, affiliated with Harvard and MIT, also claims ownership of the fundamental inventions related to CRISPR-Cas9.
Both groups claim ownership of the use of CRISPR-Cas9 in eukaryotic cells, which includes plants and animals.

The article also mentions the use of gene editing to introduce herbicide resistance and beneficial mutations in crops.
